title: A turn's first write waits until the earlier turn's moment, still being committed after a 202, has ended; at 120 s it goes and both turns are marked
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout, with TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a Postgres the run may use, run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-reporter=tap '--test-name-pattern=option A|momentsPendingOf' apps/tracy-web/test/sites-route.test.mjs packages/site/tracy-site-tabs/test/turn-open-hold.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code, the result of each test named in run.tests, and the '# p5-timing', '# p5-records' and '# p5-no-wait' diagnostic lines.
expect: S1 exits 0 and every test in run.tests reports ok, none skipped (the database was really used).

The stand's sequence through the dsh's own turn book: turn 1's /moment answers 202 with its moment running, turn 2 opens, turn 2's first write is still held 150 ms later and is let go only after turn 1's moment ended on the host (p5-timing writeReleased >= moment1Ended).

Records after it: turn 1 closed_at (the host's end of its moment) <= turn 2's first write; turn 1 head is turn 1's commit, turn 2 head is turn 2's commit; turn 1 concurrent = false and turn 2 unsealed_start = false.
When turn 1's moment ended inside its own door's wait, POST /turn names no momentsPending, tracy-web is not asked, and turn 2's first write waits under 5 ms (p5-no-wait).
POST /api/sites/:key/moment/wait answers {ended:false} while the host commits and {ended:true} once it has, with turn 1 closed under its commit by the wait itself; a malformed turn id is 400.

At the bound: release answers {released:true}; if the moment then commits, turn 1 is marked concurrent and turn 2 unsealed_start; if it commits nothing, nothing is marked. The dsh's own bound test lets the write go after ~60 ms and sends exactly one release.
The open carries waitsForMoments: true; a dsh that does not send it hears the moment named but its seal does not take that moment as harmless.

selectors.ledger: waitForMoment, releaseHold, markHeldTooLong, sealProvesStart heldBehind in apps/tracy-web/src/sites/door-follow-up.js

evidence: Local stand 09/10/2026, uiweekwp.tracy.test: turn session-5e3bc0e7…:1 closed_at 18:22:21.223 (= the host's end of moment job 32a6ced4ff6d) while turn :2 opened at 18:22:00.995; same pattern for session-2c77b352… (tasks/evidence/followups-2026-10-10/p5-turns/overlap-uiweekwp.txt).
fence: a conversation's next first write never runs while an earlier moment of it is still being committed, unless the 120 s bound ran out — and then the turns that moment may mix are marked

tests: 🔒 option A, the stand's sequence through the dsh's own turn book
option A: when the earlier moment ended in its door's wait, the next turn's first write waits not at all
option A: /moment/wait says not yet while the host commits
option A: let go at the bound, a moment that then commits marks both turns
option A: let go at the bound, a moment that commits nothing marks nothing
option A: the next open names the earlier moments still committing
option A: an older dsh that does not hold still hears the moment named
🔒 option A: the next turn's first write waits until tracy-web says the earlier moment ended
option A: no added wait at all when no earlier moment is still committing
option A: at the bound the write goes, and tracy-web is told first
